title: Plan Terms on Plans per Rental and Rentals That May Be Protected — Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan
content:
**Clause 1 — One plan per unit rental.** A Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan is attached to one storage unit rental at a time. A customer may hold one plan for each unit they rent, and there is no cap on the number of plans a customer holds. A rental may carry at most 1 plan in pending effective, active or lapsed status; a second enrollment on the same rental is not taken, and a change of level on that rental is made as a coverage change instead.

**Clause 2 — Rentals that may be enrolled.** Enrollment is taken only for a storage unit rental in reserved, active or delinquent status.

**Clause 3 — Level and unit class.** The chosen coverage level must list the rental's unit class among the unit classes eligible for that level.

**Clause 4 — Agreements that cannot carry a plan.** Parking rentals, truck rentals and business delivery services cannot carry a protection plan.

## Basis of judgement

Every point is judged from the company's system records, read before the enrollment is taken, for the rental being enrolled:

| Point | Record read | Taken when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rental status | the storage unit rental's status | reserved, active or delinquent |
| Plans already on the rental | the protection plans recorded against that rental and their statuses | none in pending effective, active or lapsed status |
| Unit class | the storage unit rental's unit class | listed for the chosen level |

## Points of judgement

- The limit counts only plans in pending effective, active or lapsed status. A plan on the rental in cancelled or terminated status is not one of them.
- The count is per rental, not per customer: a customer renting three units may hold three plans, one on each.
- A request to move an existing plan on a rental to another level is not a second enrollment; it is a coverage change on the plan already there.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A customer rents two units: one in active status with a lapsed plan on it, and one in reserved status with no plan. An enrollment on the first rental is not taken, because that rental already carries a lapsed plan; on the second rental the limit of one plan per rental does not stand in the way, and the enrollment then turns on the remaining points (the rental's reserved status is enrollable, and the chosen level must list that unit's class).
